key_insight: The paper extends algebraic flux correction from preserving affine solutions to preserving bilinear ones on quadrilateral/hexahedral meshes, matching what the finite element space can exactly represent on axis-aligned grids.
engineering_relevance: This reduces unnecessary artificial diffusion in convection–diffusion–reaction simulations, improving accuracy for FEM surrogates on structured meshes while clarifying when exact bilinear reproduction is fundamentally impossible on general quadrilaterals.
method: Derive a geometric bilinearity-preservation criterion via a lifted convex-hull condition on the mesh patch.
Obtain a sharp explicit limiter-parameter value for axis-aligned cell edges.
Characterize when mapped bilinear finite elements can reproduce bilinear fields exactly on quadrilateral meshes.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments show the proposed limiter reproduces a bilinear solution on axis-aligned grids to within nonlinear iteration accuracy, while the standard linearity-preserving limiter does not.
watch_item: The required limiter parameter sits near the upper end of the range where the fixed-point nonlinear solve remains stable, so practical robustness may be sensitive.
